components.gap: The section-6 presentation of Vaught 1961 is incomplete. (1) The source frames the never-two theorem as the answer to Raphael Robinson's question whether some complete theory has exactly two denumerable models (p. 304; p. 318 with footnote 23, which dates the question to a 1957 conversation). The handbook never states the question or that the theorem answers it: n-a-004-01.tex:122-123 only calls the two-class equivalence example 'Robinson's motivating contrast'. (2) The source's justifications inside the proof of Theorem 6.1 are dropped: T_1 has one denumerable model by Cantor's theorem (p. 318), and denumerable models of T_n are isomorphic once the constants are ignored by a theorem of Skolem [14] (p. 319). The handbook substitutes unattributed back-and-forth proofs (annex n-a-004-01.tex:138-147). It also replaces the source's sketch that T_3' is complete (pp. 319-320: completeness theorem, an elementary union and Lowenheim-Skolem, granted the three-model count) with a different game proof (annex 186-207) without presenting the source's argument. (3) The categoricity conjecture loses the source's standing and attribution: unresolved, and apparently made by a number of people (p. 320). (4) Theorem 6.1 ranges over n in omega (fn. 5, p. 304). thm:p03-vaught-finite-counts (n-a-004-01.tex:99-105) states only positive n, and lines 124-126 call positivity essential, so the n = 0 instance is excluded rather than presented. (5) The allocated subcomponents N-a-004-MAP-02 and N-a-004-MAP-04 are partial; see their gaps. Present: the never-two statement and its complete countable-model argument (MAP-01), the remaining examples, and the dated status (MAP-05). No failure condition is triggered.

components.gap: The exact original conjecture formulation is not given. Vaught (p. 320) states the conjecture for a theory categorical in some power aleph_{1+alpha} but not aleph_0-categorical, and counts its non-isomorphic denumerable models. n-a-004-01.tex:133-136 renders it as an uncountably categorical, not countably categorical theory with exactly aleph_0 'countable' models. Under the presentation's own convention (line 7: countable includes finite unless 'denumerable' is specified), that rendering also counts finite models, so it differs from Vaught's formulation for theories with finite models. The source's description of it as an unresolved conjecture, apparently made by a number of people, is also omitted. Present: the second problem, whether without CH some complete theory has exactly aleph_1 denumerable models (lines 131-133), and the separation of the later cardinal dichotomy from the never-two theorem (classification-theory.tex:192-203; n-a-004-01.tex:218-220).

components.gap: The omega-Vaught formulation is not tied to the conjecture. n-a-004-01.tex:197-205 defines vo(sigma) and calls omega-Vaught the stronger bound vo(sigma) <= alpha+omega, as opposed to merely a countable Vaught ordinal. Nothing on the route says that a countable Vaught ordinal is equivalent to sigma satisfying the (infinitary) Vaught conjecture, or that omega-Vaught strengthens that conjecture. The selected primary version says both (GRT arXiv:2606.15205v2, p. 2, the equivalence; p. 4, omega-VC). So the omega-Vaught formulation is neither related to nor distinguished from the cardinal, perfect-set and infinitary formulations as a form of the conjecture. Present: those three formulations, the infinitary-to-first-order entailment, the perfect-set/cardinality separation, and what CH does to the bare cardinal formulation (lines 141-179; annex 230-272).
